chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Leading the old Stuff Smith group in San Francisco's International Settlement
summary: Once he took over the Smith band it became his; he played the basement of a club under Mona's in San Francisco, leaving on January 6, 1942, after nearly a year.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What -- after the war, what happened? Is it true that you had your own group on the west coast too?
Yeah, after I took over the band from Stuff it became my group.
Oh, I see, so that --

And I played -- I went in the club there, nightclub there in San Francisco, at the International Settlement, down in the basement there, where I played. What did we call that then? What was the name of that damned place? Uh, well, Mona's, upstairs, was on the thing there. Mona.
Mona.
(unintelligible) everybody heard of Mona's, I don't know if you've heard about Mona's.
I've heard of Mona's.
Have you? Oh, okay. Oh, okay. Well we were downstairs in the basement, and the (sigh) what the hell was it? It was -- what did we call it? And they did pretty doggone good.
But this was -- this was the old Stuff Smith group, with you as leader.
Yeah. Uh-huh, uh-huh.
And so how long did you -- how long did you keep that group together?
Well, when I left there it was '42,
January 6th. I'd been there close to a year, I guess.
Close to a year, and then you came east?
Must have been. Yeah, came back to New York.
And this was when you formed the group on 52nd Street with Una Mae Carlisle?
(Unintelligible.)
Okay.
By golly, could have been, could have been '42.
It seems to sort of fit in, that -- the way things --
Yeah, '42 --
-- were going.
'40, and around '42, uh, '43, yeah. Must have been, because I came back and we had no job, and I had to find a job. I went there, and I heard about Philadelphia -- no. Yeah.
Yeah, this is it. So we'll pick up --
